author: Hannah Larson
title: Airline touts $39 fares, new routes in bid for Imperial service | News | thedesertreview.com
text:
EL CENTRO— Boutique Air gave a presentation to the Imperial County Board of Supervisors about its proposal to provide subsidized commercial air service to Imperial County during the regular board meeting on Tuesday, Feb. 10.
Eitan Spiegel, the Vice President of Commerce; Nadim El Khoury, the Director of Operations; and Katy Igarta, the Director of Marketing, presented on behalf of Boutique Air.
Spiegel said Boutique Air,‑based in California, started as a fire-spotting company in Shasta County and is now located in San Francisco, with a main office in Marin County. Boutique Air has been primarily doing essential air service and charter service since 2013, Spiegel said.
The company flies a Pilatus PC‑12, a Swiss-built aircraft with an eight‑ to nine‑seat passenger configuration that cruises around 300 mph.
Spiegel outlined three options in Boutique Air’s proposal — flights to Los Angeles International Airport, San Diego International Airport, and Henderson Executive Airport just south of Las Vegas, Nev. He highlighted the current utilization of the Imperial Airport as around 3,500–3,600 enplanements and said Boutique Air plans to double that figure and go beyond.
“Once people realize that they can rely upon the service and depend on it to make their treatments, to make their appointments, to make their business meetings, they will use that service,” Spiegel said.
The company’s ticket price for a flight from Imperial to San Diego will start at $39 one way, with $49 vouchers available to offset the cost of flying on the EAS carrier. Spiegel said the company partners with United Airlines, and customers can buy a single ticket on the United Airlines website or app for their total journey, and bags transferring as needed.
In response to questions from the supervisors, the Boutique Air representatives confirmed that the airline would purchase fuel in Imperial County as well as hire and train local technicians and detailers.
Supervisor Cardenas‑Singh said that a former airline, Southern Airways Express, operated nonstop flights between Imperial and Las Vegas, but that service was discontinued in late 2022. She cited multiple issues, including a bumpy flight pattern that caused the company to cancel the service.
The Boutique Air representatives said the flight pattern would not be a safety issue and that as long as pilots avoid military operations areas or restricted areas, the planes would be cleared to fly.
In late August 2025, the U.S. government sued Boutique Air, claiming the company did not conduct required drug and alcohol records checks on 21 employees hired into safety-sensitive positions, including mechanics, a pilot, and a ground safety coordinator.
According to a press release from the U.S. Attorney’s Office in the Northern District of California, the Federal Aviation Administration concluded that Boutique Air violated federal regulations and sought a civil penalty of $291,417.
Boutique Air is one of five airlines competing for the bid under the federal Essential Air Service program. The Board of Supervisors is expected to vote on the EAS contract at its Feb. 17 meeting.
